tagline: A coastal highway links a film studio’s town and formal gardens.
intro: A1A passes through Marineland and continues along the coast to Beverly Beach, where the Atlantic Ocean forms the town’s eastern boundary and the Intracoastal Waterway its western edge. Along A1A, Washington Oaks Gardens State Park combines formal gardens with preserved barrier-island habitats, including coastal scrub, hammock and tidal marshes.

The highway’s nearby history includes a retreat from the sea. At Summer Haven, north of Marineland, a road built in the 1920s added a connection to a community previously reached by boat or beach driving. Repeated storm washouts led to A1A’s relocation inland in the 1970s after Hurricane Dora; the old alignment became a county road.

Traveling south, begin with Marineland, whose Marine Studios opened in 1938 to make underwater filming possible. Washington Oaks follows, with beaches on both the Matanzas River and the Atlantic. Continue through Painters Hill to Beverly Beach, with Flagler Beach immediately beyond to the south.

moments.title: Marineland
moments.text: Marineland began as a place to put marine life on film. Marine Studios opened on June 23, 1938; two years later the town incorporated as a municipality. The attraction and town share a name, but Marineland has its own local government. The original underwater viewing world did not survive the later rebuilding: the 1938 circular and rectangular oceanariums were demolished during renovations, and their site became a parking area. The former administration building found another use as offices for the Whitney Laboratories. Former hotel and campground land became part of Flagler County’s River to the Sea Preserve.

moments.title: Washington Oaks Gardens State Park
moments.text: A gift to Florida came with instructions for the garden. Louise Powis Clark bought this property in 1936 as a winter retirement home, named it Washington Oaks and developed its formal gardens, citrus groves and house. When she donated it in 1964, she specified that the gardens retain their existing form. The park also preserves barrier-island habitats, from beach to tidal marsh. The original residence has become a visitor center with interpretive exhibits, while roses, camellias and azaleas are among the garden plants. Southern live oaks and cabbage palmettos are also among the park’s documented plants.
moments.notice: The original residence is now a visitor center with interpretive exhibits.

moments.title: Beverly Beach
moments.text: Water defines two sides of Beverly Beach: the Intracoastal Waterway on the west and the Atlantic Ocean on the east. A1A runs through this small town between Painters Hill and Flagler Beach. Its total area is 0.39 square miles, including water.
